# Avatar

A person or entity's image, falling back to initials when there is none.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |

| Registry name | `avatar` |
| Family | content |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | — |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | — | The person or entity's name. Required — it is both the fallback initials and the accessible name. |
| `src?` | `string` | — | Image URL. Omit, or let it fail, to fall back to initials. |
| `size?` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Diameter, from the `size.control.*` scale so an avatar lines up with the controls beside it. |
| `decorative?` | `boolean` | — | Marks the avatar as redundant to a name already on screen. |

### `name`

```ts
name: string
```

The person or entity's name. Required — it is both the fallback initials and the accessible name.

**Use when**

- Always. The name is what makes the fallback possible and the image describable.

**Don't use for**

- Passing an email or a user id. Initials derived from `a.hartley@` are not initials, and the accessible name would be an address.

**Accessibility** Used as the image's `alt` when `decorative` is not set. When the image is missing, the initials are shown but the full name is still what is announced — a screen reader should never hear 'AH'.

### `src`

```ts
src?: string
```

Image URL. Omit, or let it fail, to fall back to initials.

**Use when**

- A real photo or logo. The fallback is automatic, so there is no need to branch on whether one exists.

### `size`

```ts
size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = "md"
```

Diameter, from the `size.control.*` scale so an avatar lines up with the controls beside it.

**Don't use for**

- Mixing sizes within one stack of avatars — they read as a set.

### `decorative`

```ts
decorative?: boolean
```

Marks the avatar as redundant to a name already on screen.

**Use when**

- An avatar immediately beside the person's name in a row — announcing it again is noise.

**Don't use for**

- Anything standing alone. Without adjacent text the avatar is the only thing identifying the person, so hiding it removes that identification entirely.

**Accessibility** Renders `aria-hidden` with an empty `alt`. The `name` is still required, because it still produces the initials.

## Use cases

### A photo with its name beside it

A row in a member list, where the name is already text.

```tsx
<Avatar name="Ada Hartley" src={user.photo} decorative />
<span>Ada Hartley</span>
```

`decorative` because the name is right there — announcing it twice is noise. Note `name` is still required: it is what produces the initials if the photo fails to load.

### Standing alone

An avatar in a toolbar or a stack, with no adjacent name.

```tsx
<Avatar name="Ada Hartley" src={user.photo} />
```

Not decorative: the avatar is the only thing identifying this person, so it carries the name.

### No image at all

A user who has not uploaded a photo — which is most of them.

```tsx
<Avatar name="Ada Hartley" />
```

Initials are shown and the full name is announced. There is nothing to branch on: omitting `src`, and an `src` that 404s, land in the same place.
